summary: The North Carolina School Boards Association (NCSBA) urges the FCC to preserve and strengthen the E-Rate program, opposing any proposal to sunset or eliminate E-Rate support for schools and libraries. The NCSBA argues that cutting E-Rate would shift costs to local communities, competing with county budgets, and that E-Rate is essential for reliable broadband infrastructure in North Carolina schools. Local boards of education rely on E-Rate funding, which would add to county budgets if replaced. The state urges preserving E-Rate to ensure students have access to necessary technology.
